history.summary: Famous folk-deity shrine on the banks of the Valapattanam river at Parassinikadavu, Anthoor Municipality. Classified as a madappura (seat of worship) rather than a kshetram, with a distinctive three-storey white structure. Muthappan is rooted in tribal legend: he turned his friend Chantan to stone for refusing him toddy and was propitiated by Chantan's wife. Worship is non-Satvic and non-Brahminical — the primary rite is the twice-daily Muthappan Theyyam, in which devotees converse directly with the deity through the performer; offerings include toddy, fish and meat; dogs are treated as sacred, Muthappan's believed companion. All castes and religions are welcome; no dress restriction beyond removing footwear. Coordinates approximate (geocoder returned street-level match).

name: Parassinikadavu Muthappan Temple
town_description: Parassinikadavu is a riverside village on the Valapattanam river in Kannur district, North Kerala, within Anthoor Municipality about 20 km from Kannur city. It is synonymous with the Muthappan madappura and the Theyyam tradition, drawing pilgrims from across Kerala. The area is also known for the nearby Parassinikadavu Snake Park and Vismaya water theme park.
